chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from his father from Safwan from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Regarding the false testifier, what is his repentance? He said: He should pay the wealth for which he testified, to the extent of what was lost from his wealth. If it was half, or if it was a third, if he was testifying with another person with him, he pays half.
ai.seo_question: How does a false witness repent financially in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that the financial expiation (kaffarah) for a false witness involves compensating the victim for the actual loss incurred, with liability apportioned among multiple witnesses. This ruling, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq, highlights the practical application of justice in Shia jurisprudence, ensuring that the financial burden of perjury is shared proportionally among those who contributed to the wrongful deprivation of property.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 5. My father (rah) said: it was narrated to me by Sa’d b. Abdillah from Ahmad b. Abi Abdillah from his father from Safwan from al-’Ala from Muhammad b. Muslim from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said:

Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s.) was asked how a false testifier should repent. He replied, “The person should recompense the loss of wealth because of his false testimony. If the victim has lost one third of his wealth, it should be repaid. If he has lost half of his wealth, the same should be repaid and if the loss is due to testimony of two persons, they both should repay it together.”
